review_evidence: Inventoried all 1,660 primary files in this top-level-subtree unit: 569 benchmark-goals, 269 goals, 795 target-suite files and 15 library files carry mathematical statements or proofs, while the remaining 12 files are audit/gate regression fixtures or the axiom-audit executable.

Read representative goals, benchmark-goals and target-suite files, including Putnam/IMO-style theorem statements ending in sorry; these are retained because proof incompleteness does not erase statement-level prior-art value. Library/Unsorry modules were also inspected and contain reusable proved lemmas such as natural-power inequalities and integer descent steps.

All 12 selected audit/tool files were inspected completely: AuditFixtures contains synthetic sorry/axiom/native_decide/opaque cases for the audit harness, AxiomAudit/Main.lean is a Lean environment/collectAxioms CLI, and tools/gate_b/tests/fixtures contains five tiny wrong-hash or Nat toy goals used solely as Gate-B filesystem/hash regression fixtures.

rules.content_invariant: All six selected files are synthetic regression inputs for the repository's axiom/sorry audit and contain only deliberately trivial, unsound or mechanism-specific fixtures; the mathematical benchmark statements, target suites and proved library remain outside this selector.
evidence: Complete inspection covered BareSorry.lean, Clean.lean, NativeDecide.lean, NewAxiom.lean, Opaque.lean and TermSorryAx.lean.
The files deliberately exercise sorry, sorryAx, a false test axiom, native_decide and opaque-constant handling; Opaque.lean explicitly documents itself as an audit regression fixture.
rules.rationale: Remove the exact synthetic axiom/sorry audit-fixture subtree from primary mathematical search without filtering actual benchmark or library content.

rules.content_invariant: The selected AxiomAudit file is executable metaprogramming infrastructure that imports Lean, traverses Environment constants with collectAxioms and emits a report; it owns no mathematical specification, theorem development or reusable object-level formal interface.
evidence: Complete AxiomAudit/Main.lean inspection found only the audit whitelist, environment monad instance, module loading, axiom collection/reporting and CLI exit behavior.
The formal statements being audited live in retained goal/target/library modules rather than this executable.
rules.rationale: Remove repository-local axiom-audit CLI implementation from primary mathematical result slots.

rules.content_invariant: The five selected Lean files are synthetic Gate-B validation-tree fixtures: one intentionally wrong-sha theorem and four tiny Nat goals, all with sorry; they test tree/hash acceptance rather than contribute the repository's benchmark corpus.
evidence: Complete inspection covered every Lean file under tools/gate_b/tests/fixtures in this unit.
The fixture paths themselves distinguish invalid_sha_mismatch and valid_tree test cases, while the same repository separately retains its real benchmark-goals, goals and targets surfaces.
rules.rationale: Remove exact synthetic Gate-B filesystem/hash regression fixtures while retaining actual mathematical benchmark statements and targets.

summary: Reviewed the unsorry top-level formal subtree unit; retain all benchmark, target and library mathematics, excluding only content-inspected synthetic audit/gate fixtures and the axiom-audit CLI.
